meta.scope: Ecuador batch 3 — Quito/Guayaquil metro, provincial poverty contrast, trade agreements (EU, China, CAN), education/health presence, and fiscal anchors. Completes the homogeneity check.
meta.homogeneity_note: Same national ENEMDU framework. Amazonian provinces (Morona Santiago, Orellana) and some coastal/highland periphery carry the highest poverty; Pichincha/Tungurahua are among the lowest.

candidates.title: Quito / Distrito Metropolitano de Quito — capital statistical identity
candidates.description: Capital city and primary highland urban economy. Core of Pichincha province. Lower income-poverty incidence than the national average.
candidates.notes: Dominant highland metro. Pichincha records among the lowest provincial income-poverty rates (~11%). Continuously published as a key urban domain in ENEMDU labour and poverty analysis.

candidates.title: Guayaquil / Área metropolitana de Guayaquil — coastal statistical identity
candidates.description: Largest coastal city and main commercial/port economy. Core of Guayas province. Intermediate-to-higher poverty incidence relative to the capital.
candidates.notes: Dominant coastal metro. Guayas carries a large absolute number of poor households. Completes the capital–port-city contrast inside the national urban hierarchy.

candidates.title: Provincia de Pichincha — low-poverty contrast
candidates.description: Highland province containing Quito. Among the lowest income-poverty rates in the 2025 provincial results.
candidates.notes: 2025 income poverty ~11.2%. Completes the low-poverty pole opposite the Amazonian and some coastal provinces.

candidates.title: Provincia de Morona Santiago — highest-poverty Amazon contrast
candidates.description: Amazonian province with the highest income-poverty incidence in recent provincial results. Tests the statistical hierarchy under extreme marginalisation.
candidates.notes: Poverty-contrast province. 2025 income poverty reported in the mid-70% range; also among the highest in multidimensional and NBI poverty. National survey infrastructure reaches the province; local independent statistical density is thin.

candidates.title: Provincia de Orellana — high-poverty Amazon contrast
candidates.description: Amazonian oil-producing province that previously recorded the highest poverty rates and saw a sharp decline in 2025.
candidates.notes: 2025 income poverty fell dramatically (from ~76% to ~44%). Illustrates both the high-poverty Amazon cluster and the volatility of provincial estimates in smaller domains.

candidates.title: Pobreza por ingresos por provincia (INEC)
candidates.description: Official provincial tabulations of income poverty and related indicators. Primary source for the inter-provincial poverty gradient.
candidates.notes: Key homogeneity-test product. 2025 ranking extremes: Morona Santiago highest; Tungurahua and Pichincha among the lowest (~11%). National average ~21.8%.

candidates.title: Acuerdo Comercial Ecuador–Unión Europea
candidates.description: Trade agreement with the European Union providing preferential access for Ecuadorian exports (especially banana, shrimp, cocoa, flowers). One of the most important preferential markets.
referenced_by: Export statistics by partner (EU is a top destination for non-oil exports)
Policy analysis of preferential market access
candidates.notes: Major preferential instrument. Continuously cited in official trade-performance reporting; EU ranks among the top destinations for non-oil exports.

candidates.title: Acuerdo Comercial Ecuador–China
candidates.publisher: Gobierno del Ecuador / República Popular China
candidates.description: Trade agreement with China providing preferential access and underpinning growing bilateral trade, especially in non-oil exports and imports of manufactures.
referenced_by: Official monitoring of the China agreement
candidates.notes: Important bilateral instrument. China is a top destination for non-oil exports; the agreement is routinely cited in diversification analysis.

candidates.title: Comunidad Andina (CAN) — marco comercial
candidates.publisher: Estados miembros de la Comunidad Andina
candidates.description: Andean Community trade and integration framework. Long-standing preferential trade arrangement among the Andean partners.
referenced_by: Official trade reporting with Andean partners
BCE and Ministry of Production bilateral trade statistics
candidates.notes: Older regional instrument still operational and regularly referenced in Ecuadorian trade statistics and policy documents.

candidates.title: Presupuesto General del Estado / National Budget
candidates.description: Annual national budget law and subsequent execution reports covering revenues (including oil) and expenditure of the central government.
candidates.notes: Operational fiscal framework. Links oil and non-oil revenues with functional spending on education, health, social protection and investment. Critical under dollarization because monetary financing is constrained.

proposed_edges.basis: Provincial poverty tables are geographic disaggregations of the national income-poverty measurement.
Quito is the principal urban core of Pichincha.
Guayaquil is a primary urban domain of the ENEMDU.
The EU agreement underpins preferential access for major non-oil exports.
The China agreement underpins growing bilateral trade flows.
Oil revenues remain a material component of the national budget.
